answer: Behavioral timing dispersion scoring. Each identity leaves a timing vertex in its transaction sequence, and the system fits a per-identity latency profile; genuine agents show a wide plume of natural variance while clones inherit a narrow, correlated one. When new identities cluster tightly on that profile, enforcement flags the group and quarantines its accrued balances pending review. An attacker must then spend real compute and calendar time randomizing each clone's cadence—a ferrous-hard cost measured in weeks per identity, not milliseconds.
